A few years ago, I used to practice zazen by sitting on a zafu and focusing on my breathing. I would try to keep my eyes half open and looking downward a bit while staring at a wall. I'd try to keep my back erect and my hands in my lap in front of me. No music or anything, just focusing on my breathing.

Today I do basically the same thing except that I sit in a chair and keep my eyes focused on the floor in front of me. I tend to sit for 15-20 minutes at a time and I'd like to do this regularly, but in reality I don't usually do it more than once or twice a week.

The big thing for federal legalization, or even decriminalization, is that marijuana would have to be removed as a Schedule 1 drug. A lot more info here.

There are usually two ways that this can happen. A bill goes through congress, or 2/3rds of states ratify legalization.

The bill through congress is an unlikely vector, as it has been tried and shot down MANY times throughout the years. With lobbyists from Big Pharma bribing congressman to vote 'No' on any bill about it, it very likely won't happen unless lobbying somehow got banned. Even if lobbying was banned, it is still a long shot because congressmen (mainly republicans) hold onto the old 'Reefer Madness' and D.A.R.E. rhetoric. Never mind it being practically an economic miracle for Colorado (but that's partially because Colorado was the first to setup legal distribution).

The other option is for 2/3rds of states to make it legal. This one seems like it'd be more likely, albeit it is a slower process. And hell, if even 1/3rd make it legal, then that might be enough of a push for congress to legalize it nationally, or at least set up a system where it'd be decriminalized nationally and let states decide if they want it legal or not.

Most of all, there would need to be a change in public opinion, and for the most part, the polls have shown a shift in attitude already. Recent polls have shown a majority of Americans in support for full legalization and regulation. So there's that. And it could change within the next couple of elections.
